stories.title: KetchUp – Open-source SketchUp alternative built with Rust and WebGPU
stories.blurb: SketchUp has been slowly enshittified since the Trimble acquisition, so an open-source replacement built on Rust and WebGPU is exactly what the 3D modeling world needs. Runs in the browser with GPU-accelerated rendering — no install required. Worth bookmarking even if you're not a heavy 3D user; this could be the Blender moment for quick architectural sketching.

stories.title: Unlocking any car from X brand in most of the world
stories.blurb: A researcher found a vulnerability that could unlock nearly any car from a major manufacturer across most of the world — the specifics are tantalizing and the writeup is detailed. Physical security via software has been a disaster in slow motion, and this is another stark reminder. 318 comments means the HN thread is worth reading too.

stories.title: Outlook.com is rejecting email from domains without DMARC
stories.blurb: Microsoft just quietly started rejecting mail from domains lacking DMARC records — if you run any self-hosted or custom domain email, your messages may be silently dropping into Outlook's void right now. This is actionable today: check your DNS, add a DMARC record, and don't get caught out. The 346-comment thread has specific implementation advice.

stories.title: I'm not convinced the AI bubble exists
stories.blurb: A well-argued contrarian case that AI investment patterns don't match classic bubble mechanics — the author draws on historical comparisons and actual revenue data rather than vibes. With 884 comments, this is the town square debate of the day. Essential reading if you're building on or with AI tools and wondering whether the foundation will still be there in two years.

stories.title: Is Opus 5.5 nerfed? Thinking patterns changed on November 3
stories.blurb: Users are noticing a sharp change in Claude Opus 5.5's reasoning behavior since November 3rd — longer chain-of-thought seemingly truncated or altered. If you're using Claude Code or rely on Opus for complex reasoning tasks, this is directly relevant to your workflow right now. Anthropic hasn't commented yet, making the HN thread the best source of ground-truth reports.

stories.title: ChatGPT Desktop forwards your SSH agent to remote machines
stories.blurb: The ChatGPT Desktop app was found to forward your SSH agent socket to remote machines during certain operations — a serious security footgun for anyone who uses it alongside developer workflows. If you have the app installed and use SSH agent forwarding, this is a must-read before your next coding session. Classic case of AI convenience features outpacing security review.

stories.title: Chimera Vocal Synth
stories.blurb: An in-browser vocal synthesizer that can sing, speak, beatbox, and more using physical modeling — no samples, all synthesis. It's genuinely weird and expressive in ways that most web audio experiments aren't. Fire it up and spend 15 minutes making it do things you didn't think a browser could do.

stories.title: Fold Epic Paper Airplanes
stories.blurb: Beautifully designed interactive site with step-by-step animated folding instructions for genuinely impressive paper airplane designs. This is the kind of joyful, well-crafted web experience that reminds you why the web is great. Perfect lunchtime break — and the designs actually fly.

stories.title: Starship Flight 15 on 11/13 plans to catch both booster and ship
stories.blurb: SpaceX is attempting to catch both the Super Heavy booster AND the Starship upper stage with the Mechazilla arms on Flight 15 — the first time they'd pull off a full dual-catch. That's this Thursday. Set a calendar reminder; it's one of those live events where you'll want to watch.

stories.title: The same H100 costs $2.69 or $12.29 an hour depending where you rent it
stories.blurb: A methodical price comparison across GPU cloud providers reveals a 4.5x spread for identical H100 hardware — a massive difference for anyone running inference or training workloads. The repo includes provider-by-provider breakdowns you can act on immediately. If you're paying sticker price at a major cloud, you're almost certainly overpaying.

stories.title: New Research Tests Whether AI Models Know Their Own Thoughts | Quanta Magazine
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: ai, llm, mathematics, philosophy
stories.blurb: Quanta digs into new research probing whether LLMs have accurate self-knowledge — do they know what they know, or are they confabulating confidence? This is directly relevant to anyone building agentic workflows where the model's self-assessment matters for reliability. Rigorous and readable, as Quanta tends to be.

stories.title: The lethal trifecta for AI agents: private data, untrusted content, and external communication
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: security, AI, mcp
stories.blurb: Simon Willison's essential framework for thinking about AI agent security: when private data, untrusted input, and outbound comms combine, you get prompt injection attacks with real-world consequences. With MCP-based agents proliferating fast, this is required reading before you wire Claude Code into anything sensitive. The fact it's resurging on Pinboard now means people are hitting this problem in production.

stories.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
stories.blurb: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized model trained to find exploitable vulnerabilities and develop fixes while staying within authorized scope. The 'aligned' framing is doing a lot of work here, but the capability jump for security teams is real. Pairs interestingly with today's SSH agent and Secure Boot stories — the attack/defense AI race is accelerating.

stories.title: Impeccable: The missing upgrade to Anthropic's frontend-design skill
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: ai, tools, design, ai.skills
stories.blurb: A focused resource on leveling up the design quality of AI-generated UIs — specifically targeting the gap where Claude and other coding assistants produce functionally correct but visually mediocre frontends. If you use Claude Code to build web UIs, this is the missing manual for getting outputs that don't look like a first-year bootcamp project.

stories.title: GitHub - omlahore/RemoveMacAI: Turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and get its disk space back. One command, fully reversible.
stories.blurb: A one-command script to fully disable Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and reclaim the disk space it consumes — fully reversible if you change your mind. For privacy-conscious Mac users who don't want on-device AI features running in the background, this is actionable today. The reversibility story makes it low-risk to try.

stories.title: T3 Code
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: t3, app, macos
stories.blurb: T3 Code is a macOS code editor in the lineage of the T3 stack community — worth watching if you're on macOS and curious about native alternatives to VS Code or Zed. The Pinboard tagging suggests it's gained quiet traction among the macOS dev community. Check it out before it blows up.

stories.title: University libraries are being swarmed by AI bots, putting public access at risk | CBC News
stories.blurb: AI crawlers are hammering university library systems so hard that they're throttling or blocking legitimate human access — a concrete, measurable harm from the AI data race. The irony of AI training on academic resources while simultaneously breaking academic access is not lost. Expect this to accelerate the move toward bot-blocking and authenticated access walls.

stories.title: Kevin Boone: First steps in bare-metal programming using UEFI – series index
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: computers, programming, os
stories.blurb: A well-structured tutorial series on writing bare-metal UEFI programs from scratch — no OS, just you and the firmware. Goes from "what even is UEFI" to writing actual bootable code with clear progression. Pairs perfectly with today's Secure Boot exploitation story if you want to understand the attack surface from first principles.

stories.title: Borrowing a Microsoft-signed shim to abuse Secure Boot on corporate hardware
stories.blurb: A researcher demonstrates how to leverage a legitimate Microsoft-signed UEFI shim to bypass Secure Boot on corporate hardware — no exploit required, just creative abuse of the trust chain. The methodology is elegant and the implications for enterprise security are significant. A great technical writeup that deserves more attention than its score suggests.

stories.title: Writing as a thinking tool
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: writing, thinking, process
stories.blurb: A systems researcher makes the case that writing isn't just for communicating — it's how you discover what you actually think. Directly relevant to anyone using Obsidian or similar tools as a thinking environment rather than just a note dump. Short, dense, and worth re-reading after your next frustrating debugging session.
